=== usage
Usage: biab-night-shift <command>

  run       run one pass now (simulates unless the box is armed)
  status    show what is installed, armed, disabled, and how the last pass went
  arm       show the cost, ask for confirmation, then allow real passes (sudo)
            --reach pr|dev|main  how far a pass may go (default dev):
                              pr   stop at the pull request
                              dev  merge to your dev branch after the gates
                              main merge to your default branch (asks for
                                   UNLOCK MAIN)
            --unprotected-ok  also run against repos whose default branch has
                              no required review on GitHub (hook = only brake)
  disarm    go back to simulating without uninstalling anything (sudo)

  As you, not root (uses your gh login):
  dev-setup <project>   create and protect the project's dev branch
  dev-sync <project>    merge the default branch into dev when dev is behind
  promote <project>     open (or reuse) the dev -> default PR and print the
                        merge-commit command that finishes it
[rc=0]

night-shift: Arming needs all three of: a headless mode, a per-run spend cap, and a mechanical tool guard.

[rc=1]
=== arm-dev-cancel
Arming the night shift means this box will run your AI unattended,
on your subscription, while you are asleep.

Reach: dev — merges to your dev branch after CI, an independent review and your dev check; main still needs you.

What one pass can cost:
  hard cap per pass:   $2.00 implementation + $0.50 independent review = $2.50 max
  review ceiling file: MISSING OR INVALID (<box>/varlib/night-shift/guard/review-budget-usd) — passes will stop before spending until the pack is reinstalled
  wall-clock cap:      3600 seconds, enforced by systemd (TimeoutStartSec)
  passes per night:    1, one spec, no retries
  your last 7 days: not available (run the /quota skill once to build the cache)

The agent itself still stops at the pull request. Two things keep it there:
  a hook   allows only a push to its own branch and "gh pr create", and blocks
           merges, releases, the GitHub API, CI edits, root and eval. A brake.
  GitHub   a required review on your default branch that the agent, acting as
           you, cannot give itself. The lock. A pass aborts if it is missing.

At dev reach, after the agent has exited, this runner merges its PR into your
dev branch only if: the PR is the one it opened tonight, it touches no danger
zone, CI is green, an independent review finds nothing blocking, and your
.biab/dev-check.sh passes. That merge is a BRAKE, not a lock: the runner and
the agent share your account and token. Main still needs you (promote).
A project with no CI, no dev branch or no dev check stays at the pull request.

Type ARM (in capitals) to allow real passes, anything else to cancel: night-shift: not armed (nothing was written). The box keeps simulating.
[rc=1]
=== arm-pr-cancel
Arming the night shift means this box will run your AI unattended,
on your subscription, while you are asleep.

Reach: pr — stops at the pull request; you review and merge.

What one pass can cost:
  hard cap per pass:   $2.00 (--max-budget-usd)
  wall-clock cap:      3600 seconds, enforced by systemd (TimeoutStartSec)
  passes per night:    1, one spec, no retries
  your last 7 days: not available (run the /quota skill once to build the cache)

The pass stops at the pull request. Two things keep it there:
  a hook   allows only a push to its own branch and "gh pr create", and blocks
           merges, releases, the GitHub API, CI edits, root and eval. A brake.
  GitHub   a required review on your default branch that the agent, acting as
           you, cannot give itself. The lock. A pass aborts if it is missing.

[rc=1]
=== arm-pr-unprotected-notice
Arming the night shift means this box will run your AI unattended,
on your subscription, while you are asleep.

Reach: pr — stops at the pull request; you review and merge.

What one pass can cost:
  hard cap per pass:   $2.00 (--max-budget-usd)
  wall-clock cap:      3600 seconds, enforced by systemd (TimeoutStartSec)
  passes per night:    1, one spec, no retries
  your last 7 days: not available (run the /quota skill once to build the cache)

The pass stops at the pull request. Two things keep it there:
  a hook   allows only a push to its own branch and "gh pr create", and blocks
           merges, releases, the GitHub API, CI edits, root and eval. A brake.
  GitHub   a required review on your default branch that the agent, acting as
           you, cannot give itself. The lock. A pass aborts if it is missing.

  --unprotected-ok: you are switching the second one OFF. Passes will run
  against repositories with no required review, with the hook as the only
  brake. Undo with: sudo biab-night-shift arm

Type ARM (in capitals) to allow real passes, anything else to cancel: night-shift: not armed (nothing was written). The box keeps simulating.
[rc=1]
=== arm-dev-not-root
Arming the night shift means this box will run your AI unattended,
on your subscription, while you are asleep.

Reach: dev — merges to your dev branch after CI, an independent review and your dev check; main still needs you.

What one pass can cost:
  hard cap per pass:   $2.00 implementation + $0.50 independent review = $2.50 max
  review ceiling file: MISSING OR INVALID (<box>/varlib/night-shift/guard/review-budget-usd) — passes will stop before spending until the pack is reinstalled
  wall-clock cap:      3600 seconds, enforced by systemd (TimeoutStartSec)
  passes per night:    1, one spec, no retries
  your last 7 days: not available (run the /quota skill once to build the cache)

The agent itself still stops at the pull request. Two things keep it there:
  a hook   allows only a push to its own branch and "gh pr create", and blocks
           merges, releases, the GitHub API, CI edits, root and eval. A brake.
  GitHub   a required review on your default branch that the agent, acting as
           you, cannot give itself. The lock. A pass aborts if it is missing.

At dev reach, after the agent has exited, this runner merges its PR into your
dev branch only if: the PR is the one it opened tonight, it touches no danger
zone, CI is green, an independent review finds nothing blocking, and your
.biab/dev-check.sh passes. That merge is a BRAKE, not a lock: the runner and
the agent share your account and token. Main still needs you (promote).
A project with no CI, no dev branch or no dev check stays at the pull request.

Type ARM (in capitals) to allow real passes, anything else to cancel: night-shift: the mode file must be created by root — a file you can write is not a confirmation the agent cannot forge.
night-shift: re-run: sudo biab-night-shift arm
[rc=1]
=== arm-main-cancel
Arming the night shift means this box will run your AI unattended,
on your subscription, while you are asleep.

Reach: main — merges to your default branch after the same gates; no lock any more, you accepted that in writing.

What one pass can cost:
  hard cap per pass:   $2.00 implementation + $0.50 independent review = $2.50 max
  review ceiling file: MISSING OR INVALID (<box>/varlib/night-shift/guard/review-budget-usd) — passes will stop before spending until the pack is reinstalled
  wall-clock cap:      3600 seconds, enforced by systemd (TimeoutStartSec)
  passes per night:    1, one spec, no retries
  your last 7 days: not available (run the /quota skill once to build the cache)

The agent itself still stops at the pull request. Two things keep it there:
  a hook   allows only a push to its own branch and "gh pr create", and blocks
           merges, releases, the GitHub API, CI edits, root and eval. A brake.
  GitHub   a required review on your default branch that the agent, acting as
           you, cannot give itself. The lock. A pass aborts if it is missing.

At main reach the runner merges into your DEFAULT branch after the same gates.
The required-review lock is no longer the stop. The runner does not change
your branch protection: if your default branch is still locked, GitHub refuses
the merge and the pass ends at the pull request.

Type ARM (in capitals) to allow real passes, anything else to cancel: 
Type UNLOCK MAIN to accept that the review lock is no longer the stop: night-shift: not armed (nothing was written). Arm at dev reach instead with: sudo biab-night-shift arm
[rc=1]

=== arm-dev-as-root
Arming the night shift means this box will run your AI unattended,
on your subscription, while you are asleep.

Reach: dev — merges to your dev branch after CI, an independent review and your dev check; main still needs you.

What one pass can cost:
  hard cap per pass:   $2.00 implementation + $0.50 independent review = $2.50 max
  review ceiling file: MISSING OR INVALID (<box>/varlib/night-shift/guard/review-budget-usd) — passes will stop before spending until the pack is reinstalled
  wall-clock cap:      3600 seconds, enforced by systemd (TimeoutStartSec)
  passes per night:    1, one spec, no retries
  your last 7 days: not available (run the /quota skill once to build the cache)

The agent itself still stops at the pull request. Two things keep it there:
  a hook   allows only a push to its own branch and "gh pr create", and blocks
           merges, releases, the GitHub API, CI edits, root and eval. A brake.
  GitHub   a required review on your default branch that the agent, acting as
           you, cannot give itself. The lock. A pass aborts if it is missing.

At dev reach, after the agent has exited, this runner merges its PR into your
dev branch only if: the PR is the one it opened tonight, it touches no danger
zone, CI is green, an independent review finds nothing blocking, and your
.biab/dev-check.sh passes. That merge is a BRAKE, not a lock: the runner and
the agent share your account and token. Main still needs you (promote).
A project with no CI, no dev branch or no dev check stays at the pull request.

Type ARM (in capitals) to allow real passes, anything else to cancel: night-shift: armed at reach dev.
night-shift: each project needs a dev branch first, created as you (not root): biab-night-shift dev-setup <project>
night-shift: armed. Turn it off again at any time with: sudo biab-night-shift disarm
night-shift: or stop a single night without disarming: touch <box>/state/night-shift-disabled
[rc=0]
=== arm-pr-unprotected-as-root
Arming the night shift means this box will run your AI unattended,
on your subscription, while you are asleep.

Reach: pr — stops at the pull request; you review and merge.

What one pass can cost:
  hard cap per pass:   $2.00 (--max-budget-usd)
  wall-clock cap:      3600 seconds, enforced by systemd (TimeoutStartSec)
  passes per night:    1, one spec, no retries
  your last 7 days: not available (run the /quota skill once to build the cache)

The pass stops at the pull request. Two things keep it there:
  a hook   allows only a push to its own branch and "gh pr create", and blocks
           merges, releases, the GitHub API, CI edits, root and eval. A brake.
  GitHub   a required review on your default branch that the agent, acting as
           you, cannot give itself. The lock. A pass aborts if it is missing.

  --unprotected-ok: you are switching the second one OFF. Passes will run
  against repositories with no required review, with the hook as the only
  brake. Undo with: sudo biab-night-shift arm

Type ARM (in capitals) to allow real passes, anything else to cancel: night-shift: armed WITHOUT requiring branch protection. The hook is the only brake tonight.
night-shift: armed at reach pr.
night-shift: armed. Turn it off again at any time with: sudo biab-night-shift disarm
night-shift: or stop a single night without disarming: touch <box>/state/night-shift-disabled
[rc=0]

=== install-notice-armable

  Night shift installed — and switched OFF.

  What it does once you turn it on: at 03:00 it picks ONE spec you have
  validated and implements it with your AI. The agent itself stops at
  the pull request: a hook blocks merges, releases, pushes to main or dev,
  the GitHub API and CI edits — a brake. The lock is a required review on
  your default branch, which a pass checks for and refuses to run without.

  WHAT IT COSTS: a real pass spends YOUR subscription, unattended, while you
  are asleep. Capped at $2.00 ($2.50 with the review at dev reach) and
  3600s per pass, one spec per night, no retries. Nothing is spent
  until you arm it.

  Try it first — this spends nothing and tells you what it would have done:
      biab-night-shift run
      biab-night-shift status

  When you are ready:
      sudo biab-night-shift arm      (shows the cost, asks you to type ARM)
      sudo biab-night-shift disarm   (back to simulating, nothing uninstalled)

  Reach: a new arm defaults to 'dev'. After CI, an independent review and
  your .biab/dev-check.sh pass, the runner merges into a dev branch ($2.50
  max per pass). 'arm --reach pr' stops at the pull request instead. A box
  armed before this version keeps stopping at the pull request until you
  re-arm.
[rc=0]
=== install-notice-not-armable

  Night shift installed — and switched OFF.

  What it does once you turn it on: at 03:00 it picks ONE spec you have
  validated and implements it with your AI. The agent itself stops at
  the pull request: a hook blocks merges, releases, pushes to main or dev,
  the GitHub API and CI edits — a brake. The lock is a required review on
  your default branch, which a pass checks for and refuses to run without.

  WHAT IT COSTS: a real pass spends YOUR subscription, unattended, while you
  are asleep. Capped at $2.00 ($2.50 with the review at dev reach) and
  3600s per pass, one spec per night, no retries. Nothing is spent
  until you arm it.

  Try it first — this spends nothing and tells you what it would have done:
      biab-night-shift run
      biab-night-shift status

  NOTE about this box: it runs 'opencode', which cannot be armed. Arming
  requires a headless mode, a per-run spend cap and a mechanical tool guard,
  and 'opencode' does not offer all three. Simulated passes work fine and are
  genuinely useful — but on this box the night shift will stay a simulation.
[rc=0]
